rule.title: Tenant Protection Act annual rent cap (Civ. Code § 1947.12)
rule.requirement: A landlord may not raise the gross rent over any 12-month period by more than 5% plus the change in the cost of living, or 10%, whichever is lower, above the lowest rent charged in the previous 12 months, and no more than twice in 12 months.

rule.coverage_conditions: All residential rental property, including units in mobilehome parks, subject to the listed exemptions; caps increases over any 12-month period and allows at most two increases in 12 months.

rule.penalty: Owner liable for injunctive relief, damages equal to the excess rent charged, and discretionary attorney's fees, plus up to treble damages for willful, oppressive, fraudulent or malicious conduct; the Attorney General or local city attorney may enforce; three-year limitations period.
rule.quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.

rule.title: Tenant Protection Act just cause eviction (Civ. Code § 1946.2)
rule.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied residential real property for 12 months, the owner must not terminate the tenancy without just cause stated in the written notice; for no-fault just cause the owner must give one month's rent relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent.
rule.key_value: 12 months' occupancy; 1 month's rent relocation or rent waiver
rule.coverage_conditions: Residential real property occupied 12 months or more, except housing certified for occupancy within 15 years, single-family owner-occupied homes with no more than two units or bedrooms, owner-occupied two-unit properties, separately alienable property held by non-corporate owners, and deed-restricted affordable housing.
rule.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy; nonprofit hospital, religious, extended care, licensed elderly and adult residential facilities; school dormitories; housing certified for occupancy within 15 years; single-family owner-occupied residences and mobilehomes; owner-occupied two-unit structures; separately alienable property of non-corporate owners; deed-restricted affordable housing.
rule.penalty: Failure to comply renders the termination notice void; an owner who attempts to recover possession in material violation is liable for actual damages, discretionary attorney's fees, and up to three times actual damages for willful, oppressive, fraudulent or malicious conduct.
rule.interaction: Yields to local just cause ordinances adopted on or before September 1, 2019, and to more protective local ordinances adopted or amended after that date; property is not subject to both.

rule.title: Los Angeles relocation assistance for no-fault evictions under the RSO and JCO
rule.requirement: For a no-fault eviction of a tenant in an RSO- or JCO-covered unit, the landlord must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD before serving notice and pay relocation assistance within 15 days of service.
rule.coverage_conditions: All units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO) in the City of Los Angeles.
rule.exemptions: Resident-manager replacement; eviction required by a natural-disaster hazard not caused by the landlord's negligence; landlord may offset the tenant's accumulated rent. Mom and Pop properties (four or fewer units) pay reduced amounts for owner, family or manager occupancy.
rule.penalty: Failure to file the Landlord Declaration makes the eviction a violation of the RSO or JCO; a tenant may raise non-payment of relocation assistance as an affirmative defense.
rule.citation: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (L.A.M.C. §151.00 et seq.); Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (L.A.M.C. §165.00 et seq.)

rule.title: Resident Protections Ordinance relocation for demolition of Protected Units
rule.requirement: An owner demolishing a Protected Unit for new construction must file a declaration or notice with LAHD, serve the relocation notice, and pay enhanced relocation assistance to lower-income tenants rather than the standard RSO or JCO amounts.
rule.coverage_conditions: Protected Units demolished for the purpose of new construction: rent-restricted, rent-controlled (including all RSO units), lower-income-occupied within the past five years, or Ellis Act withdrawn within the past ten years.
rule.exemptions: Units that are not Protected Units or are not occupied by a lower income tenant receive the regular RSO or JCO relocation amounts instead of the RPO-enhanced amounts.
rule.penalty: Failure to comply with the RPO may result in financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of LAHD permit clearances.
rule.interaction: Owner must pay the higher of State HCA or City relocation amounts; RSO/JCO amounts must be enhanced for lower income tenants under the HCA.
rule.citation: Los Angeles Resident Protections Ordinance (L.A. Ordinances #188481, #188482)

rule.title: California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482) rent cap
rule.requirement: Annual rent increases for covered units are limited to 5% plus the regional cost-of-living change, or 10%, whichever is lower; the maximum allowable increase was 8.9% from August 1, 2024 to July 31, 2025 (previously 8.8%).
rule.coverage_conditions: Buildings older than 15 years, applied on a rolling basis. Excludes newer construction, deed-restricted affordable units, certain dormitories, owner-occupied two-unit properties, qualifying single-family homes and condominiums, and RSO units.
rule.exemptions: Units built within the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable units; certain dormitories; two-unit properties with an owner-occupied second unit; qualifying single-family homes and condominiums; units already subject to the City's RSO.
